title: The Two-Draw Well
story: A well holds {k} differently coloured stones. You draw one, then draw again.

phases.ask: How many outcomes are in the sample space if you put the first stone back?
How many if you keep the first stone out?

hints: Write a few outcomes as ordered pairs. Can a pair repeat a colour in each case?
pattern: sample space = list of ordered outcomes

title: Two Exclusive Omens
story: Omens A and B can never both appear. P(A) = {a}, P(B) = {b}.

phases.ask: P(A or B)?
P(A appears but B does not)?
P(neither)?

hints: Mutually exclusive means the circles don't overlap. What is P(AB)?
solution: AB^c = A because AB is empty.

title: Potions and Scrolls
story: In the market {a} of travellers carry a potion, {b} carry a scroll, and {ab} carry both.

phases.ask: P(a traveller carries at least one)?
P(neither)?
P(exactly one)?

hints: Draw two overlapping circles and fill in the overlap first. Then fill in each 'only' region.
solution: Exactly one = union − both = a + b − 2ab.
pattern: two-set inclusion–exclusion; fill the Venn from the inside out

title: Three Guilds
story: Of 100 villagers: {A} are in the Archers' guild, {B} in the Bakers', {Cc} in the Carpenters'. {AB} are Archers and Bakers, {AC} Archers and Carpenters, {BC} Bakers and Carpenters, and {ABC} are in all three.

phases.ask: How many villagers are in at least one guild?
How many are in exactly one guild?
A villager is picked at random. P(in no guild)?

hints: Start at the centre of the 3-circle Venn: put {ABC} there, then work outward.
'Exactly one' regions: take each circle and subtract its overlaps, but add the centre back.
solution: Union = sum of singles − sum of pairs + triple = 79.

title: The Gambler's Table
story: The rogue deals you 5 cards from a fair 52-card deck.

phases.ask: P(two pair)?
P(three of a kind, and nothing better)?

hints: Choose the ranks first, then the suits for each rank, then the leftover card(s).
Make sure the leftover cards can't accidentally make a better hand.
solution: Two pair: C(13,2) ranks for the pairs × C(4,2)² suits × 44 for the fifth card.
Three of a kind: 13·C(4,3) × C(12,2) other ranks × 4² suits.
pattern: equally likely hands: count favourable / C(52,5), ranks then suits

title: Bone Dice
story: Four fair dice are thrown together.

phases.ask: P(all four different)?
P(exactly one pair, with the other two different from it and from each other)?

hints: Use ordered outcomes (6^4 total). For one pair: which positions hold the pair? What value is the pair? What are the other two?
pattern: ordered outcomes keep everything equally likely

title: Royal Pair
story: Two cards are drawn. You win the 'royal pair' if one is a King and the other a Queen.

phases.ask: P(royal pair)?

hints: Unordered: how many ways can you pick one King AND one Queen?

title: Twin Dice Oracle
story: Two fair dice are rolled.

phases.ask: P(sum = {s})?
P(the second die shows more than the first)?

hints: Lay out the 6×6 grid of outcomes. Which cells give the sum you want?
By symmetry, how do 'second > first' and 'first > second' compare? What is left over?
solution: Ties: 6 cells; the remaining 30 split evenly: 15/36.

title: Race of the Sums
story: Two dice are rolled again and again until the sum is 6 or 7. You win if 6 comes first.

phases.ask: P(you win)?

hints: Rolls that are neither 6 nor 7 don't matter. Among the rolls that DO matter, what share are 6s?
solution: P(6) = 5/36, P(7) = 6/36. Given the game ends on a roll, P(6) = 5/11.

title: Craps in the Cellar
story: Craps: 7 or 11 on the first roll wins; 2, 3 or 12 loses. Otherwise your sum becomes the 'point', and you keep rolling until the point (win) or a 7 (lose).

phases.ask: P(you win)?

hints: Split by the first roll. For a point p, use the race idea: P(p before 7).
Points 4 and 10 behave the same, as do 5 & 9 and 6 & 8.
solution: Point p: P(first roll = p)·P(p before 7) = n_p/36 · n_p/(n_p+6).
pattern: condition on the first step + race

title: Who Draws the Ruby?
story: A pouch has {r} rubies and {b} pebbles. Asha and Bodhi take turns drawing without replacement (Asha first). The first to draw a ruby wins.

phases.ask: P(Asha wins)?

hints: Asha wins if the first ruby appears on draw 1, 3, 5, …
P(first j draws are pebbles, then a ruby) = [C(b,j)/C(r+b,j)]·r/(r+b−j).
solution: Sum over the odd draw positions 1, 3, 5, … (j even pebbles before the first ruby).
pattern: sum over the turn on which the game ends

title: Three Stones
story: A sack holds {R} red, {B} blue and {G} green stones. You grab 3.

phases.ask: P(all the same colour)?
P(all different colours)?

hints: 'Same colour' splits into three disjoint cases.
All different: one of each colour. How many ways?

title: Tagged Deer
story: A forest has {N} deer, and {T} of them wear a ranger's tag. Later, {n} deer are captured at random.

phases.ask: P(exactly {k} of them are tagged)?

hints: Split the capture: choose the tagged ones from the tagged deer, and the untagged ones from the rest.

title: The Examiner's Scroll
story: The master gives {P} practice riddles; the exam uses {S} chosen at random. You can solve {K} of them.

phases.ask: P(you can solve every exam riddle)?
P(you can solve at least {S}−1 of them)?

hints: The exam is a random subset of size S. How many subsets lie entirely inside the ones you know?
solution: At least S−1: add the subsets with exactly one unknown riddle.

title: The Sock Drawer Puzzle
story: A drawer holds n socks, 5 of them red. Two socks are drawn and P(both red) = 2/9.

phases.ask: What is n?

hints: Write P(both red) = C(5,2)/C(n,2) and solve for n.
pattern: set up the probability as an equation and solve

title: Inns of the Crossroads
story: {t} travellers each pick one of {h} inns at random, independently.

phases.ask: P(they all end up in different inns)?

hints: Count ordered outcomes. How many give all-different inns?

title: The Gambler of Méré
story: A gambler rolls one die {n} times and bets on getting at least one six.

phases.ask: P(at least one six)?
Two dice are rolled repeatedly. What is the smallest number of rolls that makes P(at least one double six) ≥ 1/2?

hints: 'At least one' → what is P(none)?
Solve 1 − (35/36)^m ≥ 1/2 for m.

title: The Gap in the Line
story: {N} adventurers line up in random order, including Asha and Bodhi.

phases.ask: P(exactly one person stands between Asha and Bodhi)?

hints: Only the pair of positions taken by Asha and Bodhi matters. How many position pairs have a gap of exactly 2?
solution: Ordered position pairs at distance 2: 2(N−2) out of N(N−1).

title: The Ring of Keys
story: A ring has {n} keys and only one opens the cellar.

phases.ask: You try keys at random, putting failed ones aside. P(the door opens on try {k})?
Careless version: failed keys go back on the ring. P(it opens on try {k})?

hints: Without replacement: by symmetry, the correct key is equally likely to be in any position.
With replacement: the tries are independent.

title: Moons of Birth
story: How many people must be gathered so that P(at least two share a birth month) ≥ 1/2? (Assume all 12 months are equally likely.)

phases.ask: Smallest group size?

hints: Compute P(all different months) for n = 3, 4, 5…

title: The Second Smallest
story: 4 tokens are drawn from tokens numbered 1–12.

phases.ask: P(7 is the second smallest number drawn)?

hints: For 7 to be 2nd smallest: how many of the drawn tokens are below 7, and how many above?
pattern: fix the special value; split the rest

title: Two Patrols
story: {m} men and {m} women are randomly split into two patrols of {m}.

phases.ask: P(both patrols have the same number of men)?

hints: The first patrol determines the second. When do they have equal numbers of men?
solution: The first patrol needs m/2 men and m/2 women: C(m,m/2)²/C(2m,m).
pattern: choose one group; the complement is fixed

title: Mismatched Boots
story: A chest holds {p} pairs of boots. You grab {k} boots in the dark.

phases.ask: P(no complete pair)?

hints: Choose which pairs you take one boot from, then which boot from each.

title: The Cloakroom Curse
story: {n} knights hand in their helmets; the cursed cloakroom returns them at random.

phases.ask: P(at least one knight gets his own helmet)?

hints: Let A_i = knight i gets his own helmet. What is P(A_i), and what is P(A_i A_j)?
Inclusion–exclusion: the k-th term is C(n,k)·(n−k)!/n! = 1/k!.

title: The Missing Suit
story: You are dealt 13 cards.

phases.ask: P(your hand is missing at least one suit)?

hints: Let V_s = no cards of suit s. Why is the answer not simply 4·C(39,13)/C(52,13)?
Inclusion–exclusion over 1, 2 or 3 missing suits.

title: Four Banners
story: You are dealt 5 cards.

phases.ask: P(at least one card from every suit)?

hints: With 5 cards and 4 suits, one suit must appear twice. Which suit, which 2 cards, and then one card from each other suit.

title: The Ace Hunt
story: A shuffled deck is turned over card by card.

phases.ask: P(the 14th card is an ace)?
P(the first ace is the 14th card)?

hints: Symmetry: is position 14 special compared to position 1?
First ace at 14: the first 13 cards have no ace, then card 14 is an ace.
solution: Any single position is an ace with probability 4/52.

title: Last Stone Standing
story: Stones are pulled one by one from a sack of {r} red and {b} blue until it is empty.

phases.ask: P(all the reds are gone before all the blues)?

hints: Reds run out first exactly when… which colour is the very last stone?
solution: The last stone is blue with probability b/(r+b).
pattern: reframe the event as 'what is last'

title: The Trickster's Dice
story: The trickster offers three dice. A = {2,2,4,4,9,9}, B = {1,1,6,6,8,8}, C = {3,3,5,5,7,7}. He lets you pick second. He picks A.

phases.ask: P(B beats A)?
Which die should you pick against A? (choose)

hints: Build the 6×6 win grid (or a 3×3 grid of distinct values) for each pairing.
Check B vs A, C vs A. Pick the one that beats A more than half the time.
solution: P(B beats A) = 4/9; P(C beats A) = 5/9; P(B beats C) = 5/9; P(A beats B) = 5/9 — no die is 'best'.
